headline: Facebook lets users type what they want to see
dek: The "algorithm" panel takes free text to adjust Feed and Reels within the same session, Meta says.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Free text for Feed and Reels
body: Facebook is letting users type, in their own words, what they want to see in Feed and Reels (Meta Newsroom).
The "algorithm" panel sits in the three-dot menu on every post, according to Meta.

points.t: List and manage the topics they want to follow (Meta Newsroom).
Answer in their own words after tapping Interested or Not interested.
See recommendations shift within the same session, the company says.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: From taps to conversation
body: Until now Facebook inferred interests from indirect signals like likes, comments and watch time, according to Meta.
The company uses large language models to read the text and blends it with the signals it already collected.

stat.cap: dots in the menu open the panel, Meta says

items.t: The company did not say which countries already have the tool.
It did not say how free text is weighed against engagement signals.
It did not say how long a written preference lasts.

caption.hook: Facebook will let users type what they want to see in Feed and Reels.
body: According to Meta Newsroom, the "algorithm" panel lives in the three-dot menu on posts and accepts free text. People can list topics of interest and answer in their own words after tapping Interested or Not interested, and recommendations shift within the same session.

The company says it uses large language models to read what people write and blend it with likes, comments and watch history. Meta did not detail which countries have the feature or how the text is weighed against behavior.
caption.cta: Would you tell Facebook in your own words what to show you?
